title: The Big Swallow (1901) Directed By James Williamson
description: The Big Swallow (1901) Director: James Williamson The Big Swallow (AKA: A Photographic Contortion) is a 1901 British silent comic trick film, directed by James Williamson, featuring a man, irritated by the presence of a photographer, who solves his dilemma by swallowing him and his camera whole. The three-shot trick film is, according to Michael Brooke of BFI Screenonline, "one of the most important early British films in that it was one of the first to deliberately exploit the contrast between the eye of the camera and of the audience watching the final film". The "tricks" used to produce the film were described in detail in Frederick A. Talbot's 1912 book Moving Pictures: How They Are Made and Worked.

title: The Bedford Incident (1965)
description: The Bedford Incident is a Cold War thriller centered around a U.S. Navy destroyer, the USS Bedford, commanded by the stern and uncompromising Captain Eric Finlander, played by Sidney Poitier.The narrative follows Captain Finlander and his crew as they patrol the North Atlantic. They receive intelligence about a Soviet submarine's presence in the area, heightening tensions. Captain Finlander’s determination to assert dominance leads him to engage in a dangerous game of cat-and-mouse with the submarine.As the situation escalates, the crew's morale begins to decline, particularly as tensions rise between Finlander and his second-in-command, Lt. Cmdr. John T. "Doc" Smith, portrayed by Richard Widmark. The crew faces ethical dilemmas and the potential repercussions of their actions as they wrestle with the pressure of military duty and the inherent risks of provocation.The conflict culminates in a tense confrontation, where Finlander pushes for aggressive action against the submarine. However, the consequences of his commanding style lead to dire outcomes, showcasing the potential tragic fallout of military aggression. The film ends on a note of ambiguity, reflecting the uncertainty and danger of Cold War tensions.

title: T-men (restored, with intro and outro) (1947, film noir, imdb score: 7)
description: T-Men is a 1947 semidocumentary and police procedural style film noir about United States Treasury agents. The film was directed by Anthony Mann and shot by noted noir cameraman John Alton. The production features Dennis O'Keefe, Mary Meade, Alfred Ryder, Wallace Ford, June Lockhart and Charles McGraw. A year later, director Mann used the film's male lead, Dennis O'Keefe, in Raw Deal. The film was endorsed by the U.S. Treasury Department: the opening credits are displayed over an image of the department's seal, then former Chief Coordinator of the department's six agencies Elmer Lincoln Irey delivers a monologue describing the objectives of those agencies and lauding their accomplishments. He describes the movie as a composite case from its files entitled "The Shanghai Paper Case".
